papers.title: A Privileged Teacher That Only Scores Cannot Search: Critique-Conditioned On-Policy Self-Distillation for Reasoning
papers.abstract: On-policy self-distillation promises to replace the sparse outcome signal of verifiable-reward RL with dense token-level credit: a teacher conditioned on the reference solution scores the student's own rollout, and the resulting distributional shift is distilled back into the policy. We investigate whether this scoring signal actually contains corrective credit. Using gold error spans in student rollouts, we test the two signals consumed by self-distillation objectives, the full-distribution KL and the token log-ratio, for two properties: whether they localize errors and whether they push probability away from erroneous student tokens. They exhibit neither of these properties nor can they reliably distinguish correct from incorrect rollouts within the same problem. We argue that this failure is structural: locating an error in a reasoning trace is itself a search problem, while a scoring teacher is never explicitly asked to perform that search. The same model, with the same privileged information, localizes errors substantially better when allowed to generate a critique. This forms the motivation for \emph{critique-conditioned self-distillation}: first generate a critique of the current rollout, then condition the scoring teacher on that critique. The resulting signal localizes errors, is corrective within error spans, and shifts probability toward tokens that initiate backtracking such as ``Wait'', ``But'', and ``Actually''. We further show that the critique is useful both at test time, where resuming a wrong rollout with the critique in context converts math problems the model cannot solve by sampling, and in cold-start GRPO, where it provides an advantage signal on prompts for which verifiable rewards alone provide none.

papers.title_zh: 只会打分却无法搜索的特权教师：面向推理的批判条件化在线策略自蒸馏
papers.summary_cn: 本文检验在线策略自蒸馏（on-policy self-distillation）所依赖的打分信号是否真的包含纠错信用：作者用学生 rollout 中的标注错误区间作为金标准，测试自蒸馏目标消耗的两种信号——全分布 KL 与 token 对数比——能否定位错误、能否把概率推离错误的 token，结果二者都不具备这两种性质，也无法在同一问题内可靠区分正确与错误的 rollout。作者认为这种失败是结构性的：在推理轨迹中定位错误本身是一个搜索问题，而只负责打分的教师从未被明确要求去做这个搜索；同一模型在拥有同样特权信息时，一旦被允许生成批判（critique），错误定位能力显著提升。据此提出批判条件化自蒸馏（critique-conditioned self-distillation）：先生成对当前 rollout 的批判，再让打分教师以该批判为条件，得到的信号能够定位错误、在错误区间内具有纠正性，并把概率推向 "Wait"、"But"、"Actually" 等触发回溯的 token；该批判在测试时可让模型接续错误 rollout 并解出采样无法解决的数学题，在冷启动 GRPO 中还能为可验证奖励无法提供优势信号的 prompt 给出优势信号。
innovations: 用 gold error spans 定量拆解在线策略自蒸馏的两种信号（全分布 KL 与 token 对数比），实证证明二者既不能定位错误也不能把概率推离错误 token，也无法在同一问题内区分正确/错误 rollout。
提出结构性解释：推理轨迹中的错误定位本质是搜索问题，而仅打分的教师未被要求执行该搜索；并用同一模型同一特权信息的对比实验，证明允许生成批判后错误定位显著变好。
设计 critique-conditioned self-distillation 流程：先对当前 rollout 生成批判，再把打分教师条件化于该批判，使蒸馏信号在错误区间具备纠正性，并显著提高 "Wait"/"But"/"Actually" 等回溯触发 token 的概率。
将批判扩展到两个下游用途：测试时用批判在上下文中续写错误 rollout，解出采样无法解决的数学题；冷启动 GRPO 中用批判为可验证奖励无信号可用的 prompt 提供优势信号。
papers.scenario_cn: 面向仅靠可验证奖励稀疏信号做 RL 训练推理模型（如数学题求解）的场景，用于提升小模型或策略模型的自蒸馏纠错效果与测试时自我修正能力，适配在线策略自蒸馏、冷启动 GRPO 等推理训练与推理时计算链路。

papers.title: Taking Tokenization off the Host for Agentic LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Agentic workloads resend long contexts that barely change between calls. Prefix caching now skips most of their prefill, yet every request must still be tokenized in full before the cache can even be consulted. Tokenization, a CPU stage long treated as negligible, becomes the largest part of time-to-first-token (TTFT), and a frontend that tokenizes for a whole GPU fleet limits how many GPUs it can feed. We present GraphTok, a GPU tokenizer that runs the entire encoding pipeline, from pre-tokenization through byte-pair encoding (BPE) merging to token-ID assembly, as one replayable CUDA graph. GraphTok reproduces the reference token IDs bit-for-bit on GPT-2, Llama 3, Qwen 2.5, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemma 3, hands short inputs to a CPU engine where the GPU cannot win, and plugs into unmodified vLLM and NVIDIA Dynamo. GraphTok encodes one million GPT-2 tokens in 1.7-3.2 ms including data transfers, and on Llama 3 it is 4.7-6.0x faster than gigatoken, the strongest CPU tokenizer. On TokTier's own single-request benchmark, it is 2.6-3.9x faster than gigatoken and up to 18.1x faster than TokTier. In vLLM with a cached prefix, it lowers mean TTFT by 2.1-2.4x. The largest gain is capacity. Within a 2 s P99 target, one Dynamo frontend with GraphTok sustains 518 requests/s of 121k-token traffic, the busiest-hour load of 56 GPUs, against 296 with gigatoken and 18.5 with the default tokenizer. Across 121k to one million tokens, this is 1.75-2.5x the load gigatoken sustains, with a P99 up to 64x lower where gigatoken's tail breaks.

在 GPT-2、Llama 3、Qwen 2.5、DeepSeek-V3、Gemma 3 五种 tokenizer 上逐 bit 复现参考 token ID 以保证正确性，并对短输入自动回退 CPU 引擎

容量收益显著：2 s P99 下单个 Dynamo 前端对 121k-token 流量达 518 req/s，为 gigatoken(296) 的 1.75-2.5 倍、默认分词器(18.5) 的约 28 倍，且 P99 尾部最多低 64 倍
papers.scenario_cn: 适用于以长且高度重复上下文为主的智能体式 LLM 在线服务（多轮工具调用、代码/文档代理等），把前端 CPU 分词从 GPU 集群吞吐的卡口上移除，落地形态是 vLLM、NVIDIA Dynamo 等推理服务系统。

papers.title: SheafPrune: Sheaf-Guided Graph Propagation for Visual Token Pruning
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models process the complete visual token sequence, increasing prefill cost even when many tokens are irrelevant to the instruction. Token-wise saliency captures limited inter-token dependence; graph-based selection instead depends on how relations govern importance propagation and ranking. We study support-constrained propagation with node-degree correction. Inspired by sheaf geometry, SheafPrune uses modality-specific maps and a sparse text--visual graph to transfer relevance, then propagates scores on a separate visual graph and corrects them for degree. It retains a hard top-$k$ subset once before the frozen language model. The selector has about $4.5$M parameters and is trained end-to-end through the frozen LLaVA-NeXT-8B backbone using only the language-modeling objective. Explicit retention-ratio conditioning lets one checkpoint serve every budget. Across four backbones, ten benchmarks and seven pruning ratios, with all baselines re-implemented under one protocol, SheafPrune achieves the best retention at $22$ of $28$ backbone--budget settings, with monotonically growing margins in the moderate-to-aggressive regime. On LLaVA-NeXT, retaining $10\%$ of visual tokens yields a $5.15\times$ net prefill speedup and an $84.0\%$ end-to-end FLOPs reduction. Together with component ablations, these results support graph-constrained importance propagation and degree correction as a design for visual token selection across the evaluated backbones and tokenization schemes, improving the trade-off between accuracy retention and inference cost. code: this https URL

papers.title_zh: SheafPrune：层束引导的图传播视觉 Token 剪枝
papers.summary_cn: 针对多模态大模型需处理后端全部视觉 token、即使大量 token 与指令无关仍抬高 prefill 开销的问题，本文指出逐 token 显著度难以刻画 token 间依赖，而图式选择的关键在于关系如何支配重要性的传播与排序，进而研究带节点度数校正的支持约束传播。作者受层束（sheaf）几何启发提出 SheafPrune：用模态专属映射与稀疏文本-视觉图传递相关性，再在独立的视觉图上传播分数并按节点度数校正，在冻结语言模型前一次性保留硬 top-k 子集。该选择器约 4.5M 参数，在冻结的 LLaVA-NeXT-8B 主干上仅用语言建模目标端到端训练，并通过显式保留率条件让单个 checkpoint 适配所有预算；在 4 个主干、10 个基准、7 种剪枝率（基线统一协议重实现）下，于 28 个主干-预算设置中 22 个取得最佳保留效果，且优势在中等至激进剪枝区间单调扩大，LLaVA-NeXT 保留 10% 视觉 token 时获得 5.15× net prefill 加速与 84.0% 端到端 FLOPs 降低。
innovations: 提出层束（sheaf）几何启发的图约束重要性传播：模态专属映射加稀疏文本-视觉图传递相关性，再在独立视觉图上传播并做节点度数校正，替代仅依赖逐 token 显著度的做法。
轻量选择器仅约 4.5M 参数，在冻结的 LLaVA-NeXT-8B 主干上以纯语言建模目标端到端训练，不需额外监督标签。
显式保留率条件（retention-ratio conditioning）使单个 checkpoint 即可服务从温和到激进的所有 token 预算，无需为每个剪枝率单独训练。
在 4 主干/10 基准/7 剪枝率、所有基线于同一协议下重实现的评测中，28 个主干-预算设置中 22 个最优；LLaVA-NeXT 仅保留 10% 视觉 token 即实现 5.15× net prefill 加速与 84.0% 端到端 FLOPs 削减，并通过组件消融验证度数校正与图传播各自的贡献。
papers.scenario_cn: 面向多模态大模型（如 LLaVA-NeXT 系列）推理服务的 prefill 降本场景：当视觉 token 存在大量与指令无关的冗余、且需按算力预算动态裁剪时，可在保持任务精度前提下大幅削减端到端 FLOPs 与首字延迟。

papers.title: BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation
papers.abstract: Distilling long-chain reasoning trajectories from large teacher models provides an effective way to improve the reasoning ability of small language models. However, existing methods typically select a fixed training set before distillation, overlooking that the usefulness of a reasoning example changes as the student evolves. This mismatch becomes especially costly when only a small number of teacher trajectories can be used for training. Besides, examples already mastered provide little new supervision, while examples far beyond the capability of student may be difficult to learn from. Training data should therefore adapt as model capability evolves, yet reliable data selection is difficult when the student is initially weak. To address these challenges, our key idea is to first establish the basic reasoning capability and then adapt the training data to the evolving capability boundary of the student. We propose BoundaryEvo, a two-stage data--model co-evolution framework. In Capability Priming, we directly distill a small set of teacher-generated long reasoning trajectories without using a separate model to judge and filter them, allowing the student to acquire an initial reasoning capability before capability-aware data selection. In Capability-Boundary Co-Evolution, we repeatedly select questions that the current student has not mastered but the expert can reliably solve, and update the training data as the student evolves. With only 1,000 training examples, BoundaryEvo consistently outperforms static and dynamic data selection baselines across 11 reasoning benchmarks, raising the original Qwen3.5-4B accuracy from 62.9 to 75.3 on IMO-AnswerBench and from 26.8 to 46.0 on AMO-Bench. The code and data will be made publicly available.

设计 Capability Priming 阶段：直接蒸馏一小批教师长推理轨迹、不使用单独模型做判断与过滤，解决学生初始能力弱时可靠数据选择困难的问题。
设计 Capability-Boundary Co-Evolution 阶段：反复筛选"当前学生未掌握但专家可可靠求解"的问题，随学生演化更新训练数据，避免已掌握样本无新监督、远超能力样本难以学习。

papers.title: DP-MIND: Differentially private memory-guided Long context Inference
papers.abstract: LLM-as-a-Service has become a dominant paradigm for accessing large language models without requiring local deployment. However, the process raises severe privacy concerns when user queries may include sensitive or confidential contexts. Differential privacy (DP) provides a principled approach to protecting such inputs, but existing DP inference methods are primarily designed for short- or moderate-context settings and struggle with million-token-scale inputs due to limited context capacity and severe utility degradation under DP perturbation. In this paper, we propose DP-MIND, a memory-guided framework that scales differentially private inference to million-token contexts. DP-MIND enables private long-context inference by locally perturbing the input and processing it chunk by chunk with a compact memory that preserves task-relevant information across the sequence. To make this memory robust to DP noise, we optimize the memory construction policy directly on perturbed inputs using reinforcement learning, guided by both final answer correctness and memory consistency. We further recover perturbation-corrupted answer spans through a local denoising module without exposing the original context to the external model. We provide theoretical privacy analysis of DP-MIND and further conduct extensive empirical analysis across multiple long-context benchmarks with context lengths up to the million-token scale, demonstrating that DP-MIND consistently outperforms existing DP and long-context inference baselines in both scalability and utility.

papers.title: JoyInside-VLM-Agent: Product-Conditioned Multimodal Policy Learning for Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Embodied agents must translate multimodal observations and user requests into executable actions while adapting to product constraints, changing goals, and execution feedback. We present JoyInside-VLM-Agent, a ReAct-style multimodal agent developed through product-conditioned trajectory construction and staged policy learning for robotic platforms and smart hardware. A closed-loop sandbox generates multimodal interaction trajectories covering goal revisions and failure recovery, which are checked against execution outcomes and semantic criteria. Supervised fine-tuning and multi-teacher on-policy distillation precede reinforcement learning with DPER (Dual-Source Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation with Token-Level Evidence Routing). DPER routes token-level evidence between a frozen privileged teacher and a privileged student sharing the rollout policy's parameters, modulating reward-derived token advantages while preserving their signs. Training rewards combine generative process evaluation, multi-judge rankings, and task-queue consistency. JoyInside-VLM-Agent achieves a BFCL v4 overall score of 77.44, exceeding the evaluated baselines; results on the other public benchmarks are mixed. On JoyInside-Devices and JoyInside-Robotics, the evaluated system, which includes domain-specific skill refinement, leads the baselines on all reported metrics. Two real-world quadruped case studies illustrate visually grounded search, replanning after execution failure, and explicit failure reporting.

papers.title: Sampling-based Kinodynamic Planning with World Models
papers.abstract: Visual world models predict the consequences of actions from images, but planning with them is typically done by optimizers such as CEM and MPPI. However, these optimizers stall on long-horizon tasks where progress requires motion the objective does not reward, such as moving around a block before pushing it. This paper revisits kinodynamic sampling-based motion planning for world models, using the learned model as the propagator of a tree search in latent space. Our key insight is that the sampling strategies devised for high-dimensional search in configuration space apply directly to the latent space of a world model, where they rapidly expand through intermediate states that myopic optimizers never sample. We present two exploration strategies for the high-dimensional latent space, nearest-neighbor-guided RRT and projection-based KPIECE, with GPU-native batched expansion for efficient device utilization. We evaluate with an off-the-shelf DINO-WM on four simulated domains and a real-world block-pushing task. Our approaches match or exceed the success rate of CEM and MPPI at up to 13.8x lower planning time in simulation, and improve the success rate by 20% on the real robot.

papers.title: CaptchaAgent: Verifiable Visual Reasoning for CAPTCHA Solving
papers.abstract: Modern reasoning CAPTCHAs require fine-grained perception, compositional relation reasoning, and grounded browser interaction. End-to-end vision-language model agents remain brittle in this setting because a missed object, incorrect count, or confused relation can propagate directly to the final action. To address this problem, we present CaptchaAgent, a structured visual reasoning framework for interactive CAPTCHA solving. Instead of predicting an action directly from a screenshot, CaptchaAgent first constructs a visual intermediate representation (V-IR) that explicitly records entities, attributes, and spatial or topological relations. A symbol-only ASCII protocol further requires the parser to commit to a concrete object set and count. Building on this global representation, localized evidence refinement revisits ambiguous regions at higher effective resolution, while counterfactual consistency verification tests whether the resulting action remains stable under task-preserving transformations. Across three proprietary backbones on Open CaptchaWorld, CaptchaAgent improves Pass@1 by 21.3-25.8 percentage points over a commercially available browser agent baseline evaluated with the same backbones. On the separate offline Oedipus-data benchmark, it further improves average Pass@1 by 9.2-12.3 percentage points over the Oedipus solver across three matched backbones. The intermediate traces show that exact counting, continuous geometry, and ordered execution remain major sources of automation difficulty for the evaluated agents, providing practical guidance for designing more resilient compositional CAPTCHAs.

papers.title: Hindsight Structured Advice Distillation: Steering Executor Agents with Advisors Trained on Their Failures and Task Characteristics
papers.abstract: Language-model agents are used for specialized work such as financial research, healthcare and law. Such agents are often capable enough for a task but still miss its details. In finance, for example, these details include which filing reports a figure or how a company discloses a metric. Retraining the agent to learn these details is expensive, and often impossible when the agent is a closed or shared system. Writing the missing know-how into the agent's prompt makes the prompt long and identical for every input, although different inputs need different guidance. We propose to learn to generate this guidance instead. A small advisor model reads each input and writes structured advice, which is appended to the prompt of a frozen executor. The advisor is trained with hindsight, following work on distillation with privileged information. On a training pool with graded answers, we analyse the executor's failures, run it under several strategies to see which one worked on each input, and let a teacher that sees the grades and the traces write the advice that would have helped. The advisor then learns, by supervised fine-tuning, to write that advice from the input alone. Because the student is a separate small model rather than the executor, it is cheap to train and adds little latency. We call this approach hindsight structured advice distillation (HSAD). On FrontierFinance, a public benchmark of expert-written financial research queries, an 8B advisor raises the qualification rate of Samaya's proprietary research agent, which already leads the benchmark's leaderboard, from 52.9% to 56.6%. This is above the agent's own high-effort configuration, at 37% lower cost per query. We study the generalization of the proposed approach, and in particular show that HSAD also improves results on WebShop, BIRD text-to-SQL and ExpertLongBench.

papers.title: LongHarness: Advancing Agentic Reasoning over 100M-Token Corpora via Stateful Evidence Management
papers.abstract: Corpus-level long-context reasoning requires agents to acquire and integrate evidence across document collections that exceed their context windows. Existing agent harnesses enable incremental access to these corpora, but acquired evidence and evolving conclusions often remain entangled in a growing interaction history. This implicit state management can lead to two coupled failure modes: unbounded exploration, where retrieval expands the interaction history without resolving decision-relevant information gaps, and evidence-state drift, where previously acquired evidence or subsequent corrections fail to inform the current conclusion. We present LongHarness, a model-agnostic harness that makes the interaction between acquired evidence and evolving conclusions explicit. Its core mechanism, Evidence-Conclusion Coevolution, uses unresolved conclusions to guide exploration toward missing information, while newly acquired evidence strengthens or revises the conclusions that directed the search. LongHarness couples this process with Evidence Lifecycle Management, which keeps accumulated evidence current and traceable throughout the interaction. Together, these mechanisms focus retrieval on remaining information needs and keep conclusions aligned with current evidence. We evaluate LongHarness on OfficeQA Pro V1 and V2, AA-LCR, and LongBench v2 using GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-Flash. Compared with direct reasoning using the same backbone, LongHarness improves GLM-5.3-Flash exact match on OfficeQA Pro from 15.8% to 60.2% on V1 and from 4.4% to 61.1% on V2. Against state-of-the-art agent harnesses, it surpasses Claude Code by 12.0 percentage points on V1 and Codex by 18.9 points on V2. papers.content_snippet: Corpus-level long-context reasoning requires agents to acquire and integrate evidence across document collections that exceed their context windows. papers.title: MADS: Multi-Agent Dialog Simulation for Robust Conversational Agents
papers.abstract: Task-oriented conversational agents remain fragile under realistic conditions, especially when users exhibit non-cooperative behavior. Existing function-calling benchmarks underrepresent adversarial conversation trajectories, thereby limiting the training resources available for developing robust agents. We present MADS (Multi-Agent Dialog Simulation), a synthetic data generation pipeline that produces structured, diverse dialogue trajectories. We inject adversarial conversation, producing validated conversation trajectories that capture realistic, unhappy paths. Using MADS, we construct MADS-Bench: a benchmark spanning six domains, 55 personas, and 1095 conversations, with approximately 66% of conversations containing failure-prone conversation scenarios. We evaluate the robustness of the trained models using a two-stage training approach that combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR).

papers.title: Masked Diffusion Language Agents for Tool-Integrated Chemical Reasoning
papers.abstract: Designing tool-integrated reasoning agent systems for complex chemical tasks remains a fundamental challenge. Although recent chemical agents have demonstrated promising performance through the integration of external tools, they are still built on the autoregressive paradigm, which is inherently constrained by causal attention and left-to-right generation. As a result, they often struggle with bidirectional molecular understanding, global coordinated tool planning and multi-source evidence integration. To address this challenge, we introduce ChemDiffAgent, the first masked diffusion language agent for tool-integrated chemical reasoning. It reformulates chemical reasoning as iterative denoising over interleaved reasoning and tool-use trajectories, enabling tool-use decisions to be jointly determined under full-trajectory context and thereby better aligning the agent's decision boundary with its knowledge boundary. We further analyze how this paradigm benefits agentic reasoning through harder infilling subproblems during training and flexible arbitrary-order decoding during inference. Then we develop a two-stage post-training framework, comprising agentic supervised fine-tuning and variance-reduced preference optimization, to enhance tool-use and reasoning capabilities. We also construct a comprehensive benchmark covering six chemistry tasks across both single-turn and multi-turn tool-use scenarios. Under matched budgets and evaluation, ChemDiffAgent consistently outperforms autoregressive agents, achieving an overall improvement of approximately 20%. Notably, our 8B model achieves performance comparable to, in some cases surpassing, significantly larger frontier models, such as GPT 5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7. Code is available at this https URL .

papers.title: TTS-Q: Perception-Guided Post-Training Quantization of Text-to-Speech Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) can clone a voice from seconds of audio. Yet the quality comes from billion-parameter diffusion transformers whose size and multi-step sampling put them out of reach of the on-device, assistive, and real-time applications that need them most. Post-training quantization (PTQ) shrinks such models without retraining, but it has been built for language and vision, not speech. At 4 bits, a strong quantizer leaves intelligibility close to full precision but consistently erodes speaker timbre, so error rates stay low while the voice drifts from the target speaker. We ask why quantization hurts speech, where the damage lives, and whether it can be repaired without retraining. To find out, we run the first 4-bit weight-and-activation (W4A4) PTQ study of a TTS diffusion transformer at 1B and 3.5B. The timbre cost comes from both the weight and the activation quantization, but only the activation part has the timestep structure a precision schedule can exploit. We therefore introduce TTS-Q, which selects hard-to-quantize items from task-matched calibration candidates and applies a budget-balanced mixed-precision schedule that assigns higher precision to late-step feed-forward activations. TTS-Q recovers timbre best at both scales, at no cost to intelligibility. Separately, the deployed calibrated-W4A4 reference reduces peak memory on GPU, providing a practical reference for resource-constrained TTS deployment.

papers.title: MHR-Router: Multimodal Heterogeneous Retrieval-Enhanced Adaptive Routing for VLM Inference
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit complementary capabilities, yet selecting the most suitable expert for a given image-question query remains challenging due to heterogeneous multimodal inputs and varying expert strengths. Existing routing approaches rely on text-based cues or static model profiles, failing to capture fine-grained visual evidence and expert-specific failure patterns. To address this, we propose MHR-Router, a multimodal heterogeneous retrieval-enhanced adaptive routing framework for VLM inference. It accurately dispatches each multimodal query to the most suitable VLM expert via local retrieval evidence. MHR-Router consists of two stages: (1) Multimodal Routing Representation, which fuses frozen multimodal features into a comprehensive query representation; and (2) Heterogeneous Retrieval-Enhanced Adaptive Routing, which retrieves expert-specific success and failure memories as local evidence and employs a shared scorer to adaptively select the optimal expert. Experiments show that MHR-Router effectively achieves heterogeneous modality routing and consistently improves accuracy over traditional baselines.

papers.title: ThinkDrag: Semantic Drag-Based Image Editing with Visual Reasoning
papers.abstract: Drag-based image editing provides an intuitive interface for spatially controlled image manipulation by allowing users to specify handle and target points. Existing methods have made substantial progress through optimization-based, one-step, and feed-forward formulations, but they often interpret drag instructions as geometric displacements. This limits their effectiveness when the desired edit depends on interpreting image content and inferring a plausible semantic transformation from sparse point constraints. We introduce ThinkDrag, a unified multimodal framework for drag-based image editing with visual reasoning. ThinkDrag is trained to associate point constraints with meaningful object- and scene-level transformations, and can optionally produce an explicit reasoning trace that interprets the intended edit before image generation. This reasoning trace improves interpretability, particularly for ambiguous drags. Drag Endpoint Markers, motivated by an analysis of cross-image attention, provide an explicit correspondence signal that grounds each drag in image space. To support this framework, we construct a supervised dataset of semantic drag transformations paired with reasoning traces and introduce DragBench++, a benchmark targeting challenging drag-based editing scenarios with reference edit solutions. Experiments show that ThinkDrag achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving generation quality and plausibility while maintaining competitive point-following precision.

papers.title: CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) reveals versatility and convenience during VLM post-training, providing dense supervision for student from teacher. However, we observed an anomaly that the distilled VLM could still answer the questions accurately even when the related visual regions were masked or replaced with noise. Building on this observation, our quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that OPD, which uses the answer as a hint, has failed to teach students to genuinely seek out and rely on visual evidence. Our theoretical analysis suggests that this failure arises from a shortcut enabled by the lack of visual constraints during distillation. To address the issue, we introduce Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation (CV-OPD), which compares teacher distributions induced by positive and negative crops while conditioning on the same student prefix and augments optimization with a margin-based contrastive constraint, which is modulated with discrepancy gating across token and sample level. Specifically, CV-OPD first introduces a negative teacher unrelated to the answer and designs a Contrastive Divergence Loss (CDL) that constrains the feature distribution of student by contrasting the positive and negative teachers, correcting how the student exploits visual regions. The CV-OPD introduces a Discrepancy Aware Gate (DAG) that uses token-level and sample-level discrepancies to select visually relevant tokens for optimization, directing the student's attention toward visual content. Extensive experiments across a broad range of fine-grained visual benchmarks demonstrate that CV-OPD substantially alleviates shortcut and consistently improves the visual reasoning capabilities of existing VLMs.

papers.title: Lossless Inference Acceleration for ASR via EAGLE-Style Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Autoregressive Transformer and Conformer models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, their sequential token generation mechanism imposes a significant bottleneck during decoding, resulting in substantial inference latency. While speculative decoding has emerged as a promising lossless acceleration technique, existing ASR-oriented approaches either suffer from low draft acceptance rates due to suboptimal draft quality or rely on specially designed external draft models, which limit their generality and practicality. To overcome these limitations, we propose EAGLE-ASR, a novel framework that accelerates ASR inference via EAGLE-style speculative decoding while strictly preserving lossless output quality. Specifically, we introduce Speech-Draft, a lightweight autoregressive module that serves as a universal draft model by jointly leveraging encoder acoustic features and hierarchical decoder representations from the target ASR model. Furthermore, we adopt a multi-step generation strategy with self-distilled data to train the Speech-Draft, enabling it to better approximate the target model's output distribution and maintain causal consistency during multi-token generation. Extensive experiments on representative Whisper and Conformer AED models demonstrate that EAGLE-ASR achieves significant lossless speedups of up to $1.9\times$ and $2.4\times$, respectively, consistently outperforming existing speculative decoding baselines for ASR. Our proposed framework further generalizes effectively to multilingual ASR and speech translation tasks, establishing EAGLE-ASR as a practical and universally applicable solution for accelerating modern ASR systems without compromising recognition accuracy.

papers.title: Adaptive DHiSparse: Speculative Decoding over a Load-Adaptive KV Hierarchy
papers.abstract: Long-context serving runs out of KV memory before the hardware reaches its useful throughput. HiSparse stores history in host memory and fetches only the selected entries, but it uses one cache budget at every load and does not handle draft-model speculative decoding such as DSpark and DFlash2. We present Adaptive DHiSparse, which supports speculative decoding over hierarchical sparse KV and adapts residency to load. It protects the required working set, retains additional history while GPU memory is spare, and recovers the rest through exact fused retrieval. DSpark and DFlash2 keep their proposal and acceptance rules: queries share missing-row retrieval, draft KV uses a window-bounded ring, and verification staging is reused across layer groups. At 100K context and concurrency 128, GLM-5.3 with DFlash2 delivers 793 output tokens/s per decode GPU, 1.45$\times$ HiSparse and 1.27$\times$ non-speculative adaptive serving. Held to the same latency bounds as HiSparse, it sustains up to 4$\times$ the concurrency and 2.3 to 3.7$\times$ the output, depending on the per-token bound. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at 500K context and concurrency 512, Adaptive DHiSparse with DSpark delivers 1.85$\times$ the output of resident serving with DSpark. In a load step, optional residency reduces host fetches from 14.2% to 1.4% of selected rows at low load and releases memory under pressure.

papers.title_zh: 自适应 DHiSparse：在负载自适应 KV 层级上的投机解码

papers.title: CORAL-KV: Compact Cross-Layer Prediction and Residual Coding for Autoregressive Video KV Caches
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models maintain a growing attention key-value (KV) cache, making memory a key bottleneck for long video generation. Recently, clustering-based quantization has emerged as an effective method to compress video KV caches by grouping similar key and value vectors then quantizing residual errors. However, when later frames attend to the compressed history, small reconstruction errors can compound as the video grows. Beyond the within-layer similarity exploited by clustering, we find strong dependencies across cache layers in video models. This motivates Coral-KV - Calibrated Offline, Residual-coded, and Adapted Locally - a KV-cache compression framework that uses cache states in each layer to predict keys and values in subsequent layers, then quantizes the remaining prediction residuals. We construct compact block-diagonal-plus-low-rank (block-DPLR) predictors: block-diagonal components model channel relationships within each attention head, while a global low-rank term models dependencies between heads. Coral-KV exposes a flexible fidelity-memory trade-off: it can reuse its predictors across videos or refit lightweight block-diagonal predictors to the current video for higher fidelity. Across extensive evaluations on both HY-WorldPlay and MAGI-1, our reusable configuration improves PSNR over QVG-4 by 0.32 dB and 4.95 dB, respectively, while using 48% and 37% less cache memory. Against QVG-Pro, our video-adapted configuration improves MAGI-1 PSNR by 3.77 dB while using 33.7% less cache memory. Coral-KV also maintains higher reconstruction fidelity over extended generation and reduces temporal discontinuities while retaining comparable generation latency.

papers.summary_cn: 本文针对自回归视频扩散模型在长视频生成中 KV 缓存随帧数持续增长、成为显存瓶颈的问题：现有基于聚类的量化压缩在后续帧回看压缩历史时，微小重建误差会随视频长度累积放大。作者发现视频模型除层内相似性外还存在强跨层依赖，据此提出 Coral-KV（Calibrated Offline, Residual-coded, Adapted Locally）框架，用每层的缓存状态预测后续层的 key/value，仅对预测残差做量化；其预测器采用紧凑的块对角加低秩（block-DPLR）结构，块对角分量建模单个注意力头内的通道关系，全局低秩项建模头间依赖。在 HY-WorldPlay 与 MAGI-1 上的实验显示，可复用配置相比 QVG-4 分别提升 PSNR 0.32 dB 与 4.95 dB，同时少用 48% 与 37% 缓存显存；视频自适应配置相比 QVG-Pro 在 MAGI-1 上提升 PSNR 3.77 dB 并少用 33.7% 缓存显存，且在更长生成中保持更高重建保真度、减少时间不连续，生成延迟基本持平。

papers.title: $L_0$ Feature Selection via Monte Carlo Tree Search in High-Dimensional Financial Regression
papers.abstract: Feature selection is a central problem in high-dimensional financial regression, where large numbers of engineered variables and strong correlations among predictors reduce model stability and interpretability. $L_1$ regularization (Lasso) is widely used for sparse regression, but its shrinkage can be restrictive when informative signals are spread across correlated variables. Exact sparse regression avoids this shrinkage but requires solving a combinatorial optimization problem that is computationally difficult and is typically fit to minimize in-sample rather than out-of-sample error. This paper presents a feature selection framework based on Monte Carlo Tree Search with Generalized Nested Rollout Policy Adaptation (GNRPA). Feature selection is formulated as a sequential decision process, and candidate subsets are scored by their out-of-sample validation performance rather than training error. The method also supports a lexicographic objective accounting for subset size and multicollinearity. papers.title: DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs
papers.abstract: Low-bit inference on accelerators with native 4-bit support requires quantizing both weights and activations to realize the full throughput gains these formats provide. While post-training weight quantization has been extensively studied, activation quantization remains considerably more challenging and typically requires calibration data. In this work, we introduce DUALQUANT, a dual-scale, calibration-free post-training quantization framework that directly minimizes the weight-reconstruction Mean Squared Error (MSE) and, as an immediate by-product, yields per-channel activation rescalings prior to activation quantization. Our key observation is that the scaling factors obtained by minimizing weight-reconstruction error provide effective activation rescalings, enabling competitive activation quantization without calibration data. We formulate DUALQUANT as a non-differentiable weight-reconstruction problem and develop an efficient solver based on variable splitting and block coordinate descent, where each subproblem admits a closed-form update. DUALQUANT provides a unified algorithm supporting a wide range of formats, including the full MX family and NVFP4. To our knowledge, DUALQUANT is the first dual-scaling method to formally support MX and NV block formats. Across Llama and Qwen models evaluated on WikiText-2, C4, and zero-shot downstream tasks, DUALQUANT matches or exceeds the accuracy of calibration-based SmoothQuant across most models and formats, and substantially outperforms calibration-free baselines, with large gains for MX and NV block formats. We validate these gains with a real packed W4A4 inference path for Llama-3.1-8B on an RTX 4090. The resulting implementation closely matches the accuracy of fake quantization while delivering up to 2.61x memory reduction and up to 2.46x throughput speedup over BF16.

papers.title: Auditing VLM Benchmarks from Existing Evaluation Runs
papers.abstract: Every evaluation run of a vision-language model (VLM) already produces per-question artifacts (predictions, judged correctness, metadata) that leaderboards reduce to a single score and then discard. We reuse those artifacts to audit the benchmark itself, and add an audit layer to VLMEvalKit: six detectors that run as post-processing over saved outputs, plus one additional text-only rerun with visual inputs removed, emitting a per-question report. The layer reports per-question findings together with aggregate audit statistics; for the headline quantities, it attaches permutation-null excess where applicable, interval estimates for proportions, and sensitivity to the model pool. Auditing MMStar, a benchmark curated specifically so that the image is indispensable, with three models, we find zero aggregate accuracy gain from the image on 20.2% of its questions. An item-matched permutation null accounts for 17.0%, leaving a +3.2 pp excess (corrected permutation p = 0.001). This excess is concentrated in the mathematics and science categories and is absent from coarse perception, a localization consistent with knowledge substituting for visual evidence; confirming that mechanism would require item-level review. A second detector flags 134 questions on which every model that answered in parseable form picked the same non-gold option, and these candidates peak in the perception categories, whereas the zero-gain excess is largest in mathematics and science & technology. Replacing the LLM judge with exact string matching changes no conclusion, and every scoring discrepancy between the two traces to one model whose free-form answers a parser cannot read. On a binary yes/no benchmark the detectors measurably fall out of calibration, a scope boundary that we measure and report. The audit layer, the prediction artifacts and the generated reports accompany this submission.

papers.title_zh: 从既有评测运行中审计视觉语言模型基准
papers.summary_cn: 论文指出现有 VLM 评测在跑完一轮后会产生大量逐题产物（模型预测、判定是否正确、元数据），但排行榜只把它们压缩成一个总分就丢弃，这些产物其实可以反过来审计基准本身。作者在 VLMEvalKit 上新增一个审计层：6 个检测器对已保存输出做后处理，外加一次去掉图像输入的纯文本重跑，输出逐题报告；对关键量还附带置换零假设超额、比例区间估计和模型池敏感性。在专为“图像不可缺”而构建的 MMStar 上，用 3 个模型审计发现 20.2% 的题目上图像没有带来任何总体准确率增益，题目匹配的置换零假设可解释其中 17.0%，仍余 +3.2 个百分点超额（校正后置换 p=0.001），且该超额集中在数学与科学类目、在粗粒度感知类目上不存在，与“语言知识替代视觉证据”的机制一致（作者指出确认该机制仍需逐题人工复核）。第二个检测器标出 134 道题，其上所有能解析出答案的模型都选了同一个非金标选项，这些可疑题在感知类目达到峰值，与零增益超额在数学/科学技术类目最大的分布恰好相反。把 LLM 判官换成精确字符串匹配不改变任何结论，两次评分之间的全部差异都可追溯到某一个模型的自由文本答案无法被解析；而在二元 yes/no 基准上检测器会可测量地失准，作者测量并报告了这一适用范围边界。审计层、预测产物与生成报告随投稿一并发布。
innovations: 提出“回收评测产物做基准审计”的范式：不改模型、不重跑全量评测，只在已保存的逐题输出（预测/判定/元数据）上做事后审计，把排行榜丢弃的细粒度信号重新利用起来。
在 VLMEvalKit 中落地可复用的审计层：6 个事后检测器 + 1 次移除视觉输入的纯文本重跑，自动产出逐题报告与聚合审计统计。
把统计稳健性做成审计报告的标准输出：对头条指标同时给出置换零假设超额（permutation-null excess）、比例区间估计和模型池敏感性，而不是只报一个点估计。

给出跨模型一致性检测器：找出“所有可解析作答的模型都选同一个非金标选项”的 134 道可疑题，其类目分布（感知类峰值）与零增益超额的类目分布（数学/科学技术最大）相反，形成交叉印证。

papers.scenario_cn: 适用于 VLM 基准的维护方与榜单运营方在发榜前做自查：定位“图像可有可无”的冗余题和疑似金标错误的题目，用于修题或分层报告。也适用于用 MMStar 等基准做模型选型的研究者与工程师，用来判断某次分数提升究竟来自真实视觉理解还是语言知识先验。评测工具链可把该审计层集成进评测框架，以几乎零额外推理成本（仅一次去图重跑）实现基准健康度的持续监控；构建新多模态基准时也可用它验证“图像确实不可缺”这一设计承诺是否成立。此外可用于评测方法论与审稿场景，用置换零假设、区间估计、判官替换等可复现口径检验榜单结论的稳健性。

papers.title: LETHE: Defending against Unauthorized Image-to-Video Generation via Value Diversity Collapse
papers.abstract: Image-to-video (I2V) diffusion models can animate a single reference image into high-quality, subject-consistent videos, posing threats of misuse as anyone can turn personal photos into fabricated videos without consent. A promising solution is to proactively add an adversarial perturbation to the image before release, such that videos generated from it would be unfaithful or visually corrupted. However, due to an insufficient understanding of what governs how subsequent frames read the reference image in modern I2V models, existing protections struggle to offer strong protection under common perturbation budgets. In this paper, we approach the problem by exploring this underlying reading mechanism. Through a convex geometric analysis, we theoretically identify the spread of the reference value vectors as a key factor governing this reading process, and empirically find that even a mild contraction of this spread can severely degrade the generated video, making it an efficient lever for protection. Guided by this insight, we propose LETHE, a novel protection method that directly disrupts this reading process. LETHE pairs two complementary objectives, where a value collapse objective drives the reference value vectors toward uniformity, while an attention attraction objective draws subsequent frames toward these collapsed tokens to amplify corruption. We further construct two human-centric I2V protection benchmarks and conduct extensive experiments with multiple modern I2V models, which demonstrate the state-of-the-art protection performance and versatility of LETHE.

papers.title: Algebraic Integer Quantization for Machine Learning Applications
papers.abstract: In this article, we propose algebraic integer number formats (AINF) as a framework for highly configurable and accurate compressed computation. A key property of AINF is its straightforward reduction to purely integer arithmetic, enabling error-free multiply-accumulate operations. We develop a matrix multiplication engine that exploits this property, obtaining performance within a predictable factor of the most efficient numerical counterparts on modern hardware accelerators. Another key advantage of AIQ is the freedom to select algebraic integers tailored to the numerical characteristics of a given use case, offering optimization opportunities that are fundamentally unavailable in floating-point or fixed-point formats. Motivated by these properties, we introduce algebraic integer quantization (AIQ), a lossy compression format for large language model (LLM) inference, and provide results demonstrating that AIQ achieves competitive accuracy compared to the industry-standard MX format across a diverse set of models and benchmarks at equivalent bit-per-parameter budgets. The experiments presented in this article employ algebraic integers of degree two (quadratic integers); generalizations to higher-order and, in particular, multidimensional algebraic integers promise even greater computational advantages and remain a promising direction for future work.

innovations: 提出代数整数数值格式（AINF）与代数整数量化（AIQ），利用代数整数可精确归约为纯整数算术的性质实现无误差的乘加运算，规避浮点舍入误差。
基于 AINF 实现矩阵乘法引擎，在现代硬件加速器上以可预测的常数因子代价逼近最高效数值实现的性能。
AIQ 可按具体用例的数值特性自由挑选代数整数（实验使用 degree-2 二次整数），提供浮点与定点格式根本不具备的优化自由度。
在同等每参比特预算下，在 Llama/Qwen 等模型与 MMLU、HellaSwag、ARC 等基准上取得与工业标准 MX 格式相当的精度，并指出高阶与多维代数整数是更具算力优势的后续方向。
papers.scenario_cn: 面向大模型推理部署中的低比特权重压缩与高吞吐矩阵乘需求，适用于希望用纯整数运算替代浮点、在不牺牲精度的前提下降低加速器算力与显存开销的推理引擎、量化工具链及定制数值硬件。

papers.title: Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) extends on-policy distillation (OPD) by routing domain-specific data to specialized teachers, integrating their capabilities through dense token-level supervision on student-generated trajectories. However, domain routing only distinguishes the supervision sources for different domains; updates from all domains still act on shared parameters. When teachers differ substantially in response style and domain expertise, supervision that is effective in isolation may still lead to persistent gradient conflicts and capability degradation during joint optimization. To address this challenge, we propose Cross-Teacher Guarding for MOPD (Road MOPD), which introduces non-routed teachers as auxiliary cross-domain critics on the same student trajectories and coordinates multi-teacher supervision through token-level credit assignment and gradient updates. Specifically, cross-teacher-guided credit assignment uses teacher agreement to strengthen token-level corrections jointly supported by the teachers and attenuate conflicting signals; preventive multi-teacher gradient projection uses auxiliary gradients from the same trajectories to constrain potentially conflicting updates and adaptively controls projection strength to retain target-domain learning signals. In experiments, Road MOPD mitigates degradation in the disadvantaged domain, gains over 5 percentage points under high conflict, and improves overall performance in low-conflict and three-domain settings.

papers.title_zh: 超越领域路由监督：多教师在线策略蒸馏中的跨教师守护
papers.summary_cn: 多教师在线策略蒸馏（MOPD）按领域把数据路由给专门的教师模型，但领域路由只区分监督来源，各领域的更新仍作用在共享参数上，当教师回答风格与专长差异较大时，联合优化会出现持续梯度冲突与能力退化。论文提出 Road MOPD，把非路由教师作为同一学生轨迹上的跨域评论者，通过跨教师引导的信用分配（以教师一致性强化共同支持的 token 级修正、衰减冲突信号）与预防性多教师梯度投影（用同轨迹辅助梯度约束潜在冲突更新、自适应调节投影强度以保留目标域学习信号）来协调多教师监督。在 Qwen3-1.7B/4B 学生模型上，于 AIME24/AIME25/HMMT25、MedQA/MedXpertQA/MedMCQA/SuperGPQA、HumanEval/MBPP/LiveCodeBench 等基准评测，Road MOPD 在 Math×Medical、Code×Medical 与三领域设置中均优于 ExOPD、Open-MOPD、CaMOPD、PCGrad 等基线，高冲突场景提升超过 5 个百分点。
innovations: 提出 Road MOPD 框架：将非路由教师作为辅助的跨域评论者（cross-domain critic），在相同的学生生成轨迹上协调多教师监督，解决领域路由只区分监督来源、参数更新仍相互冲突的问题。
跨教师引导的信用分配（cross-teacher-guided credit assignment）：以多教师的一致性作为信号，放大被多个教师共同支持的 token 级修正，并衰减相互冲突的监督信号。
预防性多教师梯度投影（preventive multi-teacher gradient projection）：复用同一轨迹上的辅助教师梯度来约束潜在冲突的更新，并自适应控制投影强度以保留目标域的学习信号。
在 Qwen3-1.7B/4B 学生上覆盖数学、医学、代码三类评测：Math×Medical 与 Code×Medical 的二领域平均分在四种设置中均为最高，超出最强基线 0.72–2.89 分，高冲突条件下提升超过 5 个百分点，并缓解劣势领域的能力退化。
papers.scenario_cn: 面向需要把多个领域专家模型能力合并进单个通用大模型的后训练落地，适用于数学、医学、代码等多专长能力融合，以及教师风格差异大、直接联合蒸馏易出现能力掉点的训练流水线。

papers.title: Branching On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories, but a single trajectory realizes only one continuation at each decision, limiting supervision coverage under a finite sampling budget. We propose BranchOPD (Branching On-Policy Distillation), which selects informative decision points using student uncertainty and teacher-student disagreement, resamples student-policy continuations from shared prefixes, and applies token-level teacher supervision to both main trajectories and branches. BranchOPD operates at token-level decisions in mathematics and within-turn decisions in agent tasks. Shared-prefix reuse reduces student-generated token costs by approximately 19% on ALFWorld and 31% on WebShop relative to seven independent trajectories. We also introduce protocol-boundary repair (PBR), which uses targeted supervision under protocol constraints to mitigate repetition and wasted generation. BranchOPD outperforms Vanilla OPD and Multi-Rollout OPD (n=7) across all evaluated benchmarks, with gains over Vanilla OPD of 18.55 percentage points in mean mathematics accuracy over 16 sampled answers (avg@16) and 13.8 points in mean ALFWorld ID/OOD success. Mechanistic analyses and selection ablations show that branching at uncertain decisions expands subsequent behavior coverage and outperforms random selection and turn-initial branching.

papers.title_zh: 分支式在线策略蒸馏
papers.summary_cn: 论文针对在线策略蒸馏（OPD）中单条轨迹在每个决策点只实现一种续接、导致有限采样预算下监督覆盖不足的问题，提出 BranchOPD（Branching On-Policy Distillation）。该方法利用学生模型不确定性与师生分歧挑选信息量大的决策点，从共享前缀重采样学生策略续接分支，并对主轨迹与分支统一施加 token 级教师监督，在数学任务上作用于 token 级决策、在智能体任务中作用于回合内决策。共享前缀复用相比独立采样 7 条轨迹，在 ALFWorld 与 WebShop 上分别减少约 19% 与 31% 的学生生成 token 开销；同时提出协议边界修复（PBR）在协议约束下做定向监督以缓解重复生成与无效解码。BranchOPD 在所有评测基准上优于 Vanilla OPD 与 Multi-Rollout OPD（n=7），相较 Vanilla OPD 在 16 次采样平均数学准确率（avg@16）上提升 18.55 个百分点，ALFWorld 的 ID/OOD 平均成功率提升 13.8 个百分点。

共享前缀复用显著降低生成成本：相比 7 条独立轨迹，ALFWorld 学生生成 token 减少约 19%、WebShop 减少约 31%。
提出协议边界修复（PBR），在协议约束下施加定向监督，缓解重复生成与无效生成。
机制分析与选择消融表明：在不确定决策点分支可扩展后续行为覆盖，且优于随机选择与回合起始处分支。结果上相较 Vanilla OPD 在 avg@16 数学准确率提升 18.55 点、ALFWorld ID/OOD 平均成功率提升 13.8 点。
papers.scenario_cn: 适用于在有限采样预算下让小模型通过在线策略蒸馏高效学习数学推理与交互式智能体（ALFWorld、WebShop 类工具/网页操作）能力的训练场景，尤其需要降低多轨迹采样 token 成本并抑制重复、无效生成时。

papers.title: CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation (OPD) requires aligning teacher and student sequences before their scores can be compared. Decoded-text alignment provides such correspondence at the chunk level, but leaves a distinct problem unresolved: credit alignment. A chunk-level signal specifies how much a span should change, but not how that signal should be distributed across student tokens, while tokens without teacher correspondence remain unconstrained. We propose CAST (Chunk-aware credit Assignment with Selective Token Anchoring), a shift-or-stay framework that addresses both issues. For aligned chunks, CAST redistributes each chunk's advantage across student tokens using predictive uncertainty and local teacher-signal smoothness, emphasizing learning opportunities supported by locally consistent teacher feedback while preserving the chunk's total advantage. The resulting weights exactly solve a KL-regularized credit-allocation problem. For unaligned positions, CAST selectively anchors the student to its initial policy through a KL penalty, limiting drift where teacher supervision is unavailable. Because credit assignment is separated from chunk construction, CAST also applies to punctuation-defined or fixed-length chunks under shared tokenization. Across six mathematics, science, and code benchmarks, CAST improves the average over the strongest evaluated baseline by $2.45$ and $1.32$ points for cross-tokenizer transfer from Qwen3-8B to Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B, respectively, and by $2.10$ points for shared-tokenizer transfer to Qwen3-1.7B.

papers.title_zh: CAST：面向跨分词器在线策略蒸馏的信用对齐
papers.summary_cn: 论文聚焦跨分词器在线策略蒸馏（OPD）中，解码文本对齐虽能给出 chunk 级对应关系，却遗留“信用对齐”问题：chunk 级信号只说明某段应改变多少，未说明该如何分配到各学生 token，且无教师对应的 token 仍缺乏约束。为此提出 CAST（Chunk-aware credit Assignment with Selective Token Anchoring）这一 shift-or-stay 框架：对已对齐 chunk，按预测不确定性与局部教师信号平滑度把 chunk 优势重分配到学生 token，突出局部一致的教师反馈所支持的学习机会，同时保持该 chunk 总优势不变，且所得权重精确求解一个 KL 正则化信用分配问题；对未对齐位置，则通过 KL 惩罚选择性地把学生锚定到其初始策略，限制无教师监督处的漂移。由于信用分配与 chunk 构造解耦，CAST 也适用于同一分词器下按标点或固定长度构造的 chunk。在六个数学、科学与代码基准上，CAST 相较最强基线，Qwen3-8B→Mistral-7B 与 Qwen3-8B→Llama-3.1-8B 的跨分词器迁移平均分别提升 2.45 与 1.32 点，迁移到 Qwen3-1.7B 的同分词器场景提升 2.10 点。
innovations: 提出 CAST（Chunk-aware credit Assignment with Selective Token Anchoring）shift-or-stay 框架，在解码文本 chunk 对齐基础上解决跨分词器 OPD 的信用对齐问题。
对已对齐 chunk，用预测不确定性与局部教师信号平滑度将 chunk 优势重分配到学生 token 并保持总量守恒，且证明所得权重精确解一个 KL 正则化信用分配问题。
对无教师对应的未对齐 token，采用 KL 惩罚选择性锚定到初始策略以限制漂移，防止监督缺失区域发散。
信用分配与 chunk 构造解耦，兼容标点定义或固定长度 chunk 及同分词器场景；在六个数学/科学/代码基准上，Qwen3-8B→Mistral-7B、→Llama-3.1-8B 跨分词器迁移平均提升 2.45 与 1.32 点，同分词器迁移到 Qwen3-1.7B 提升 2.10 点。
papers.scenario_cn: 适用于教师与学生模型分词器不一致时的在线策略蒸馏部署（如 Qwen 教师蒸馏到 Llama/Mistral 学生，或蒸馏更小模型），解决解码文本对齐下信号无法落到具体学生 token、以及无对应 token 缺乏约束导致的训练不稳定问题。

papers.title: ForcingBooster: Adaptive Patch-wise Denoising for Fast Autoregressive Video Diffusion
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models have become a leading approach to real-time interactive video generation and video world modeling. However, existing methods typically allocate computation uniformly across space when generating the next video chunk, updating all patches with the same denoising schedule and number of function evaluations. This ignores the spatial heterogeneity of video content: static, simple, or recurring regions are often easier to denoise, while other regions require further refinement or additional context. A uniform budget thus leads to redundant computation on easy patches, whereas reducing the fixed step count can leave difficult patches insufficiently refined. We introduce \methodname{}, a general framework that dynamically allocates denoising steps to individual patches: easy patches stop early to improve efficiency, while difficult patches receive more refinement steps. This design accelerates generation with negligible quality degradation. Our method is compatible with most existing few-step autoregressive diffusion models, requiring only a lightweight routing module with modest training. Experiments demonstrate that \methodname{} reduces the total number of denoising steps applied across video patches by about 50\% while maintaining visual quality comparable to the four-step baseline.

papers.title_zh: ForcingBooster：面向快速自回归视频扩散的自适应分块去噪
papers.summary_cn: 自回归视频扩散模型已成为实时交互式视频生成与视频世界建模的主流路线，但现有方法在生成下一个视频块时对空间一视同仁：所有 patch 共用同一套去噪调度和相同的函数评估次数。这忽略了视频内容的空间异质性——静态、简单或重复出现的区域本就好去噪，另一些区域却还需要进一步精修或补充上下文。统一预算的结果是：简单 patch 上产生冗余计算，而单纯压低固定步数又会让困难 patch 精修不足。ForcingBooster 提出按 patch 动态分配去噪步数的通用框架：简单 patch 提前停止以提升效率，困难 patch 获得更多精修步数，从而在视觉质量几乎不下降的前提下加速生成。该方法与多数现有的少步自回归扩散模型兼容，只需一个轻量路由模块和少量训练即可接入。实验显示，在视觉质量与四步基线相当的情况下，视频各 patch 上的总去噪步数减少约 50%。
papers.innovations: ① 从空间异质性出发，提出 patch 级自适应去噪步数分配框架，把计算预算从易去噪区域转移到真正需要精修的困难区域；② 用轻量路由模块学习每个 patch 是否继续去噪，训练开销小，即插即用；③ 与主流少步自回归视频扩散模型兼容，不改变原有生成范式；④ 在保持四步基线视觉质量的前提下，将视频 patch 上的总去噪步数削减约 50%。
papers.scenario_cn: 适用于实时交互式视频生成与视频世界模型推理加速，尤其是算力有限、要求低延迟连续生成视频 chunk 的场景；当视频内容在空间上高度非均匀（大面积静态背景叠加局部高动态主体）时，节省的计算量最为可观。

papers.title: Golden Anchor for Video Generation
papers.abstract: Video generation supports digital content creation, with applications in virtual avatars, AI-driven filmmaking, interactive game engines, and world models. State-of-the-art systems achieve controllability primarily through image-to-video (I2V) generation, in which an injected anchor image determines the identity, composition, and style of the resulting video. In modern pipelines, this anchor is synthesized by a text-to-image (T2I) generator. This raises a largely overlooked question: Are images obtained directly from the T2I model truly suitable for current video models? Our analysis shows that anchor aesthetic and quality scores are weakly correlated with downstream video quality. The structure-and-texture score is negatively correlated with I2V video quality in both the visual and motion dimensions. Fine-tuning the T2I model on an image reward accordingly yields anchors with visibly denser structural and character detail: they score higher on image metrics, yet lower the video reward on every I2V model we test and change downstream motion unpredictably. We therefore introduce Golden Anchor Learning (GAL), to our knowledge the first framework for learning golden anchors by optimizing a T2I generator with downstream video feedback. GAL evaluates candidate anchors through the videos they induce under a frozen I2V model and converts video rewards into image-level preferences for DPO fine-tuning of the T2I generator. On all four I2V models, GAL raises the VBench average by $2.97\%$--$8.46\%$ over the untuned generator. The rendered clips also score higher under VideoReward-Overall, and their extracted frames under HPSv3 and UniPercept. GAL yields consistent motion gains across all four I2V models, as measured by a $5.62\%$--$38.24\%$ increase in VBench dynamic degree. Although GAL is trained only on HunyuanVideo-1.5 renders, these gains extend to the other three I2V models.

papers.title: Learning Representations to Guide Pixel Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Visual representations are largely developed for understanding, yet what makes them useful for generation remains unclear. We study this question in pixel diffusion transformers and uncover two key insights. First, better representation quality does not necessarily translate into greater generative utility, as externally aligned semantics can be progressively lost during pixel synthesis. Second, architectural separation with specialized pixel decoders mainly redistributes semantic and spatial modeling, without necessarily yielding representations better suited to generation. These insights suggest that a useful generative representation must be both properly formed and actively exploited. Motivated by these insights, we introduce Representation Guidance (RG), which directly forms and exploits internal representations while retaining a plain Transformer architecture. A low-dimensional bottleneck forces generation-relevant information into a compact representation, which is then explicitly used to guide decoder generation by modifying the flow-matching target according to its induced prediction offset. RG learns clearer semantic and spatial structure while scaling efficiently in both parameters and computation. On ImageNet 256x256, RG-L/16 with only 459M parameters outperforms substantially larger pixel diffusion transformers, while RG-XL/16 achieves an FID of 1.55. RG further reaches an FID of 1.74 at 512x512 and extends to text-to-image generation, achieving 0.89 on GenEval and 87.1 on DPG-Bench.

papers.title: Beyond Temporal Proximity: Explanatory World Models for Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Generative Recommenders increasingly use Reinforcement Learning (RL) to optimize outcomes that may appear hundreds or thousands of interactions after a decision. Standard RL propagates reward according to temporal proximity rather than explicit relevance, attenuating the signal assigned to distant but important actions and creating a source of sample inefficiency. We introduce Explanatory World Models (EWM), an attribution framework that uses explanations to identify the earlier events that plausibly contributed to a realized outcome. We instantiate EWM with a frontier language model and use its explanations as learning signals using a conservative hierarchical operator that recursively redistributes reward while preserving the undiscounted episode return. To investigate what constitutes a useful explanation, we operationalize three complementary variants inspired by Halpern's actual causation, Lombrozo's explanatory simplicity, and Deutsch's hard-to-vary explanations. We evaluate EWM on two controlled long-horizon RL benchmarks, a public sequential-recommendation benchmark, and an industry-scale generative recommender. On Crafter and WordCraft, EWM substantially outperforms PPO and LaRe, with its largest gains when rewards are most delayed. On KuaiRand, EWM outperforms SFT and LaRe offline and A2C online. Finally, in an offline evaluation of an industry generative recommender, EWM considerably improves Recall and increases behavioral proxies. These results suggest that explanations can provide structured and reusable credit for learning from delayed outcomes.

papers.title: GLIMPSE: Global-Local Indexing with Multi-Precision Spectral Encoding for Explorable Video World Models
papers.abstract: A camera-controlled video world model must keep a scene consistent when the camera returns to it. Memories that render stored features into the target frame can turn depth and pose errors into ghosting or duplicated structure. Positional transport avoids that resampling by relocating a historical patch's address rather than its content, but assigns full positional precision even to inaccurate projections. We present GLIMPSE, a global-local memory interface with band-wise multi-precision coordinates and geometry-conditioned spectral attenuation to reduce sensitivity to inaccurate projected addresses. Local patch memory supplies view-specific appearance, while recurrent global memory provides scene context. Footprint-guided retrieval selects historical patches under a fixed local read budget. Under matched retrieval and read budgets, GLIMPSE improves geometric correspondence and photometric consistency over deterministic positional transport.

papers.title_zh: GLIMPSE：面向可探索视频世界模型的全局-局部索引与多精度谱编码
papers.summary_cn: 论文针对相机可控视频世界模型中“相机返回同一场景时如何保持一致、避免重影或结构重复”的记忆读取问题：把历史特征渲染进目标帧会因深度与位姿误差产生重影，而位置搬运（positional transport）虽通过搬运历史 patch 的地址而非内容来规避重采样，却对不准确的投影地址仍赋予完整位置精度。作者提出 GLIMPSE，一种带分频段多精度坐标与几何条件化谱衰减的全局-局部记忆接口，以降低对错误投影地址的敏感度。其局部 patch 记忆提供视角相关外观、循环全局记忆提供场景上下文，并以足迹引导检索（footprint-guided retrieval）在固定局部读取预算内挑选历史 patch。在检索与读取预算对齐的条件下，GLIMPSE 相比确定性位置搬运提升了几何对应与光度一致性。

papers.title: JANUS: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models
papers.abstract: Long-horizon autonomous research has shown promise in accelerating scientific progress through sustained cycles of hypothesis generation, implementation, and validation. However, this Generate-Execute-Feedback paradigm relies on reactive trial-and-error, where costly and time-consuming executions introduce severe feedback delays, throttling evolutionary progress under explosively expanding search space. To address this challenge, we propose JANUS, a framework that unifies future outcomes forecasting and past experience reflection through a Predict-Verify-Evolve loop driven by a co-evolving world model. Within an evolving graph, the research agent proposes candidates while world model scores them by forecasting value improvement, information gain, and exploration utility, then accordingly selects, refines, or prunes branches prior to execution. After receiving ground-truth feedback, JANUS distills experience into evolving skills: hierarchical skills for research agent, exploration-strategy skills for world model, and their coordination protocols. This mechanism enables continual co-evolution: the research agent sharpens candidate generation while the world model refines its predictive judgment over extended horizons. Extensive evaluations on MLS-Bench-Lite and real research tasks demonstrate that JANUS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving both higher evolving efficiency and ceiling.

papers.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
papers.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) aims to transform interaction experience into persistent improvements, yet external feedback is costly and world-model predictions may become unreliable as policies evolve. We introduce RSI-Anything, a domain-general framework built on JEPA-Anything that uses predictive world models to guide action and learning-data selection. Observed feedback drives policy or workflow improvement and conditional world-model adaptation, while component and compatibility checks govern the retention of updated policy-model pairs. Across diverse computational and scientific domains, RSI-Anything demonstrates substantial gains. In code repair, with the coder fixed, success increases from 26.3% with a static verifier to 29.2% through predictive selection and 31.2% after world-model adaptation, at comparable test usage. Graphical user interface (GUI) evaluations showed higher task completion, while average actions decrease by 39.4%. Across five successive policy versions, laboratory-planning scores more than double from 21.80% to 46.01%. In reaction optimization, RSI-Anything achieves 96.15% mean best observed yield versus 82.16% for Bayesian optimization under the same 40-experiment budget. An end-to-end immune-science application further connects workflow evolution and predictive modeling with therapeutic hypothesis generation. These results demonstrate how predictive world models and retained system updates enable recursive improvement across diverse environments.

papers.title: SimVTA: Simulation-Grounded Video-Trajectory Alignment for Driving World Action Models
papers.abstract: Driving world action models (WAMs) learn from paired trajectories and future observations. Post-training with reinforcement learning allows the policy to explore alternative trajectories and improve planning using driving rewards. However, driving logs contain future videos only for the recorded trajectories, leaving these alternatives without corresponding visual supervision. Thus, we introduce SimVTA, a simulation-grounded post-training framework that combines trajectory optimization with video supervision. First, we sample candidate trajectories for each observation and use a real-world simulator (e.g., World Engine) to render future videos for high-reward candidates in real-world scenes reconstructed with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). This provides trajectory-matched supervision independent of the model's own predictions. Under a limited rendering budget, we prioritize video supervision for higher-error futures among these rendered candidates. Finally, we optimize trajectory planning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and use a flow-matching loss on the matched videos to update shared representations. At inference time, the model predicts trajectories directly, without simulator calls. On NAVSIM v1, applying SimVTA to a WAM initialization improves PDMS from 86.2 to 91.3 (+5.1). It achieves 88.2 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 and an average HD-Score of 38.8 in closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM. Ablations show that updating shared representations with video supervision improves planning, while prioritizing higher-error futures among high-reward trajectories further improves performance.

papers.title: 3DRAG: 3D-Native Object Drag Editing with Generative Models
papers.abstract: The rapid progress of 3D generative models has made 3D asset creation increasingly accessible. However, achieving intuitive, precise, and interactive user control, such as point-based drag editing, remains challenging. Existing 3D drag methods either rely on slow 2D diffusion priors, such as Score Distillation Sampling, or directly warp geometry, often causing multi-view inconsistency and topological artifacts. In this paper, we present 3DRAG, a training-free framework that executes precise drag editing natively within the explicit 3D latent space of large-scale generative models, without SDS-based optimization or iterative point tracking. To ensure geometrically plausible deformations, 3DRAG explicitly extends the drag displacement field into 3D space, incorporating an Occupancy-Aware Winner-Takes-All (OA-WTA) strategy to robustly handle sparse geometries. Furthermore, we introduce a generative editing pipeline that explicitly transforms latent representations via the 3D displacement field. By fully leveraging the model's generative capabilities, it achieves smooth geometric deformations while maintaining the object's identity. To further transfer original geometry and texture with high fidelity, we propose Logits-Level Token Fusion, which accurately injects source information into the destination region. To evaluate 3D point-based editing, we construct a novel dataset featuring diverse 3D assets and complex multi-point drag instructions. Quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that 3DRAG achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing existing baselines in drag accuracy, geometric fidelity, and unedited region preservation.

papers.title: Don't Guess, Just Ask: Evaluating Interactive Requirement Clarification for Repository-Level Software Development
papers.abstract: As LLMs become increasingly capable of implementing software, a critical bottleneck emerges: whether they truly understand what users want. Users often begin with vague intent, leaving important requirements to be clarified through interaction. In repository-level development, misunderstandings can propagate and cause costly rework. However, existing benchmarks typically evaluate implementation from complete specifications or underspecified requests, overlooking pre-coding requirement clarification. Prior clarification studies mainly focus on function-level tasks. It therefore remains unclear how well LLMs can transform vague intent into clear requirements through interaction and how this capability affects subsequent code generation. We introduce ReqClarifyBench, an interactive requirement clarification benchmark for repository-level software development. It contains 341 tasks spanning game, miniapp, and web development, each with a vague user intent, a human-validated requirement document, and code evaluation artifacts. We employ LLM-based user simulators with diverse personas derived from real-world conversations. We evaluate six LLMs in terms of clarification effectiveness and generated requirement document quality. Results show that stronger clarification effectiveness does not necessarily translate into higher document quality, and performance varies substantially across user personas. We also find that coding-agent harnesses do not further improve requirement document quality compared with their base LLMs. These findings offer insights for building LLM-based end-to-end software development systems.

papers.title: Exploring Attention Sinks in Text-to-Image Transformers from Diffusion and Autoregressive Models
papers.abstract: Attention sinks are tokens or positions that consistently receive disproportionate attention mass, often beyond what their semantic content would suggest. Despite extensive study in large language models, their behavior and functional relevance in text-to-image (T2I) Transformers remain largely unexplored. To fill this gap and better understand how text-to-image Transformers allocate and route attention, we explore this phenomenon of text-to-image transformers across bidirectional diffusion models and causal autoregressive models. Specifically, we explore whether attention sinks exist, where they emerge, and how they functionally influence generation. Through systematic attention analysis and targeted interventions, we identify that attention sinks emerge in both bidirectional diffusion and autoregressive models but exhibit distinct patterns. The autoregressive model concentrates attention on the first and global-scale tokens, whereas the bidirectional models develop sinks near modality boundaries, within text regions, and at spatial corners. Moreover, these patterns vary across generation stages and are localized to a sparse subset of layers and heads. To assess their functional relevance, we perturb sink-related heads and token positions. It turns out that perturbing sink-ranked heads produces larger average changes than non-sink comparisons, while some sink-position perturbations have limited effects on bidirectional model scores. We further introduce register tokens to redistribute attention sinks and find that several configurations preserve or modestly improve generation performance. Overall, attention sinks are architecture-, inference-stage-, and component-dependent phenomena, providing a basis for mechanistic analysis and principled attention design in text-to-image transformers.

papers.summary_cn: 本文首次系统研究文本到图像（T2I）Transformer 中的“注意力汇”（attention sinks）现象，即持续接收远超其语义内容应有注意力权重的 token 或位置。作者同时覆盖双向扩散模型与因果自回归模型，通过系统的注意力分析与定向干预，发现两类架构都存在注意力汇但模式截然不同：自回归模型把注意力集中在首个 token 和全局尺度 token 上，而双向模型则在模态边界、文本区域内部以及空间角落处形成注意力汇，且这些模式随生成阶段变化并仅局限于稀疏的层与注意力头上。作者进一步通过扰动与引入 register token 验证其功能意义，发现扰动 sink 排名靠前的头带来的平均变化大于非 sink 对照，而部分 sink 位置的扰动对双向模型评分影响有限。

papers.title: GeopoliticalQA: Benchmarking Retrieval and Generation over Intelligence Reports
papers.abstract: Geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports constitute a rich source of expert knowledge and have increasing value in the current political climate, but their heterogeneity and analytical complexity pose challenges for retrieval-augmented question answering. We introduce a benchmark for grounded question answering over 415 open-source geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports, comprising 5,525 document-grounded question-answer pairs spanning factual, inferential, comparative, and risk-oriented questions. papers.title: Improving Semantic Coverage in AI Test & Evaluation through Generative Augmentation
papers.abstract: In test and evaluation (T&E) of AI models, evaluators typically have access only to a held-out test dataset and no knowledge of the training data or its semantic composition. If critical input conditions---such as time-of-day, weather, or scene location---are underrepresented in this test dataset, T&E results can be misleadingly due to this semantic coverage gap. We propose a three-stage generative AI pipeline to detect and fill such semantic gaps without requiring ground-truth labels of these semantics. First, vision-language models (VLMs) perform zero-shot binary labeling of semantic factors, and an embedding-space clustering step identifies which semantics most affect downstream model behavior. Second, diffusion-based image-to-image models transform existing covered images into the underrepresented semantic domain, preserving scene content while augmenting high-level appearance. Third, statistical analysis of the augmented image embeddings verifies that the synthetic imagery improves dataset coverage before it is incorporated. Crucially, the synthetic data is used only to enrich the test set and no model retraining is performed for T&E. We validate the full pipeline on both image classification and object detection under day/night semantic gaps, showing that the augmented test datasets better distinguish models with and without exposure to the missing semantic, thereby yielding T&E conclusions that more closely match those of an ideal, fully covered dataset. papers.title: Incremental Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Human-in-the-Loop Decision Support
papers.abstract: We introduce iRAG, a human-in-the-loop decision-support system combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with Hybrid Decision-Making. Unlike conventional RAG systems, relying on static Knowledge Bases (KBs), our proposal addresses settings where the KB is initially empty and is progressively populated through human decisions. The system stores previous decisions as retrievable precedents and moves from silent observation to evidence-grounded contestation and, finally, to autonomous handling with abstention. Against an independent baseline, iRAG matches final-decision error under 10% drift without retrieval decay and reduces it under 40% drift across all configurations. Retrieval decay improves performance on changed knowledge while increasing error on stable knowledge, evidencing a stability--plasticity trade-off rather than a general advantage. Human oversight is an architectural provision of the workflow; its usability with real human users remains to be evaluated.

papers.title: Not All Correct Fixes Run Alike: An Empirical Study of Patch Performance in Repository-Level Issue Resolution
papers.abstract: Repository-level issue-resolution benchmarks such as SWE-bench evaluate submitted patches primarily based on whether they pass the correctness tests, leaving the runtime performance of different test-passing patches largely unexplored. Evaluating patch performance is essential but challenging since designing performance workloads for each benchmark instance is costly. However, these benchmarks already provide a natural candidate: the built-in \emph{FAIL\_TO\_PASS} (F2P) tests, which exercise the behavior affected by the issue fix. We therefore investigate whether the provided F2P tests can be repurposed to evaluate patch performance. Overall, we choose four frontier models, Claude Opus~5, GPT~5.6, DeepSeek V4 Pro, and Qwen~3.8 Max, paired with SWE-agent to resolve the pre-filtered measurable corpus from verified splits of SWE-bench and SWE-bench-Live, yielding 262 cases with at least two different correct solutions, including the developer ground-truth patch. We then measure each solution's runtime performance in instruction count and wall-clock time on the native F2P test, and use Welch ANOVA instead of the RSD proposed in prior work as a more robust statistical discrimination criterion. We find that this methodology exhibits notable discrimination capability in runtime performance and identifies performance differences among patches in almost half of the instances. Our empirical study shows that the runtime performance of generated patches is independent of the issue resolution rate of LLMs, with nearly reversed model rankings. The case study also shows that the performance analysis reveals architectural regression in some patches that the correctness evaluation overlooked. These findings suggest that resolution rate does not adequately characterize LLMs' capability for repository-level issue resolution, motivating future evaluations to consider patch performance alongside it.

papers.title: SCCGBench: Executability-Oriented Evaluation for Real-World Web Service-Call Code Generation
papers.abstract: LLM-generated service-call code is increasingly important for service computing, where developers rely on large language models (LLMs) to compose services and invoke third-party services. However, current approaches have not yet evaluated the invocation and execution of services in the actual code environment. To support execution-grounded evaluation, we present the Service-Call Code Generation Benchmark (SCCGBench), a benchmark of 3,135 traceable and decontamination-filtered RapidAPI call functions from real GitHub repositories. SCCGBench uses redacted-intent generation to reduce circular leakage and introduces Mock, Robust, ParamF1, and host-, endpoint-, method-, and parameter-level diagnostics. Mock denotes a virtual-execution hit that simultaneously matches the gold host, endpoint, and HTTP method, while Robust further requires status checking and exception handling. We evaluate six code LLMs and one non-neural retrieval baseline under intent-only, retrieval-augmented, and gold-documentation Oracle settings. Results show that models often generate syntactically correct or superficially similar HTTP-request code but achieve low Mock success in the intent-only setting; the strongest evaluated model obtains only 3.76% Mock. Under the gold-documentation Oracle settings (C3 and C5), Mock reaches 88.73%--90.52% for the open-source models evaluated in RQ2 and 76.47%--81.86% for DeepSeek-V4-Pro, whereas sparse and dense retrieval remain far below this oracle level. The findings indicate that service/API grounding is the main bottleneck: Mock is dominated by host, endpoint, and method alignment, while ParamF1 separately reveals parameter-alignment errors. SCCGBench provides an execution-grounded benchmark for Web service invocation, API recommendation, service-interface retrieval, endpoint grounding, and reliable service-call automation.

papers.summary_cn: 论文指出现有大模型生成服务调用代码的评测，尚未在真实代码环境中验证服务是否真能被调用与执行。为此作者提出 SCCGBench：一个包含 3,135 个取自真实 GitHub 仓库、可追溯且经去污染过滤的 RapidAPI 调用函数的基准。该基准采用“意图脱敏生成”以减少循环泄漏，并引入 Mock、Robust、ParamF1 以及 host、endpoint、method、parameter 多层级诊断指标。其中 Mock 表示一次虚拟执行同时命中金标准 host、endpoint 与 HTTP 方法，Robust 还额外要求状态码检查与异常处理。作者在“仅意图”“检索增强”以及“金标准文档 Oracle”三种设定下评测 6 个代码大模型与 1 个非神经网络检索基线。结果显示：模型常能写出语法正确或表面相似的 HTTP 请求代码，但在仅意图设定下 Mock 成功率很低，最强模型也只有 3.76%；在 Oracle 金标准文档设定下，开源模型 Mock 可达 88.73%–90.52%，DeepSeek-V4-Pro 为 76.47%–81.86%，而稀疏与稠密检索仍远低于该 Oracle 水平。结论是服务/API 的落地对齐（grounding）才是主要瓶颈：Mock 由 host、endpoint、method 的对齐主导，ParamF1 则单独揭示参数对齐错误。
papers.innovations: 1) 提出首个以可执行性为核心的真实 Web 服务调用代码生成基准 SCCGBench，规模为 3,135 个来自真实 GitHub 仓库、可追溯且经去污染过滤的 RapidAPI 调用函数；2) 采用“意图脱敏生成”（redacted-intent generation）降低循环泄漏带来的评测虚高；3) 设计 Mock、Robust、ParamF1 及 host/endpoint/method/parameter 多层级诊断体系，把笼统的“能否跑通”拆解为可定位的失败维度；4) 在仅意图、检索增强、Oracle 三种设定下横向评测多类模型与检索基线，证明 API grounding 而非语法正确性才是核心瓶颈。
